minutes.headline: Commissioners voted to re-adopt the Tighe & Bond plan for one Lancaster Avenue treatment plant, and heard of huge water main cost overruns.
minutes.summary: The Water District Commissioners reviewed and voted on personnel policy changes, approved prior minutes, and re-voted the Tighe & Bond master plan with clearer wording for a single treatment facility on Lancaster Avenue. The superintendent reported major added costs on the state-permitted water main job, hydrant flushing, pilot testing, and new federal PFAS limits that create a tight timeline.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the warrants were signed and requested that the warrants being signed be read aloud; told they were payroll and payables warrants and electric bills.

votes.motion: Approve the changes to the personnel policies and benefits.
Accept the minutes of March 27 and March 30.

Approve the Tighe & Bond recommended alternative design: one treatment facility on Lancaster Avenue to treat the Hickory Hills well and the Lancaster Avenue wells per section 4.4 of the master plan, with an estimated budget number.

budget_items.what_was_said: Motion cited an estimated budget for the Lancaster Avenue treatment facility serving Hickory Hills and Lancaster Avenue wells. Stated as not a vote to spend, but to follow the plan.

budget_items.topic: Water main job added costs from state permit
budget_items.what_was_said: State permit requirements not in the contract produced massive added costs; the district will try to renegotiate with the contractor.
Contractor price for filling old pipe under roadway was very high, exceeding available contingency.
The district borrowed for the job and the contract came in a little over a lower figure, leaving small contingency.
Restricted state permit work hours produced a change order that may be eliminated if a town support letter lets hours be extended.
A commissioner said a special meeting would be needed to appropriate more money for the roughly four thousand feet of pipe.
The job is funded entirely by borrowing with no outside funding; terminating would still incur contractor costs.
New EPA limits apply to all sources, requiring treatment; three years to decide and meet the rule by year five.
Policy references last year's voted buyback program and requires proof of alternate coverage if an employee declines district insurance.

decisions.decision: Add a date to the personnel policy showing when it was modified, and commissioners to initial the bottom of the page.
Superintendent to return at the next meeting with an update on the water main job costs and options such as a reduced scope or lining instead of replacement.
Commissioners chose not to put a numeric definition on chronic absenteeism; left to superintendent discretion.

what_happened.line: Commissioners moved to re-adopt the Tighe & Bond plan for one treatment facility on Lancaster Avenue serving the Hickory Hills and Lancaster Avenue wells; the outcome was not audible.
The superintendent reported that state permit requirements not in the contract added major costs to the water main job; no action was taken and he is to return with options.
The water main job is funded entirely by borrowing, and a commissioner said a special meeting would be needed to appropriate more money.
Commissioners moved to approve personnel policy and benefit changes, adding a modified date and commissioner initials to the policy; the outcome was not audible.
The superintendent said new federal PFAS limits apply to all sources and require treatment, with three years to decide and a rule to be met by year five.

why_it_matters: The treatment plant plan and the water main overruns are both paid for by borrowing, which can reach water rates and what customers are asked to approve.
A special meeting to appropriate more money for the main, and the PFAS treatment timeline, could put new spending and borrowing decisions before district voters.
